 JD JD Published: November 5, 2026 AndreyPopov Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 If the taxes on your home went up over the past year in Montana, it may have something to do with the Homestead Act .  And if you didn't file for it, like me, then yes, your taxes on your home went up.  Way up.
 via GIPHY 
 There is the possibility of seeing a little relief from those big numbers in the letter you received from the state for property taxes .  A refund may be available to eligible homeowners who qualify and signing up for it is simple with the state.
 Get our free mobile app File Soon for Your 2026 Property Tax Refund in Montana
 To receive the tax refund, first determine if your home qualifies.  If you are unsure whether you received the credit, the state of Montana offers the ability to check your enrollment status.  If you have received the tax credit already, you are good to go, and nothing further is needed.
 dondesigns dondesigns READ MORE:  Clearing a 1000 Miles of Montana Trails - See What It Takes with US Forest Service 
 However, if you didn't receive it, you may be eligible for a refund beginning on January 1, 2027.  Homeowners should meet the following criteria from the state's website in order to file for a refund:
 You owned the property during the 2026 tax year
 The property was your primary residence for at least seven months in 2026
 Your 2026 property taxes and all prior-year property taxes are paid in full
 How to Claim Your Refund with the State of Montana for 2026 Property Taxes
 If your home qualifies, your refund covers the missed benefit of the 2026 reduced homestead rate.  Before you sign up for the refund, make sure you have your Social Security number available, and you will also need your properties geocode.  You can find instructions on how to do so here .
 AndreyPopov AndreyPopov Once the signup portal opens, the state also will require a phone number or email that you may be reached at and the address of which to send the refund to.  Want to see if you qualify?  Stay updated at the state's website here .  You can also search for frequently asked questions here .
